senses.definition: A small, simple house, often in the woods.
senses.example: We stayed in a cabin near the lake.

senses.definition: An enclosed area for people in a ship, airplane, or other vehicle.
senses.example: An attendant checked the airplane cabin before takeoff.

senses.definition: A place that keeps a copy of information so a computer may use it again quickly.
senses.example: The browser could read the image from its cache.

senses.definition: An element that is part of strong bones and teeth and helps nerves and muscles do their jobs.
senses.example: The nutrition label shows that the yogurt provides calcium.

senses.definition: A chart or computer tool that shows days, weeks, and months.
senses.example: We marked the first day of camp on the calendar.

senses.definition: To speak loudly to get someone’s attention, or to reach someone by phone.
senses.example: Please call me when the game is over.

senses.definition: To give or use a name for someone or something.
senses.example: We call our cat Button.

senses.definition: An attempt to reach someone by phone or a shout to get attention.
senses.example: I missed a call from my aunt.

senses.definition: To decide you have done enough for the day and stop.
senses.example: We had painted the whole first wall, so we decided to call it a day.

senses.definition: Lettering written with care as a form of art.
senses.example: The invitation was decorated with blue calligraphy.

senses.definition: Quiet, still, or free from strong worry.
senses.example: The lake was so calm that we could see clouds in it.

senses.definition: To make someone or something less upset or active.
senses.example: Music helped calm the nervous puppy.

senses.definition: The breaking away of ice from the edge of a glacier to form floating pieces.
senses.example: Calving formed several new icebergs at the front of the glacier.

senses.definition: Color, shape, or pattern that makes a living thing hard to see in a place.
senses.example: The octopus used its skin color as camouflage against the rocks.

senses.definition: A place or program where people stay or spend time doing things together, often outdoors.
senses.example: We made kites at day camp.

senses.definition: To stay outdoors for a while, often sleeping in a tent.
senses.example: Our family likes to camp by the lake.

entries.pronunciation: kan (container), kan or kuhn (be able to)

senses.definition: To be able, allowed, or free to do something.
senses.example: I can read the sign from here.

senses.definition: A metal container that holds food, drink, or something else.
senses.example: I found a can of beans on the shelf.

senses.definition: To seal food in a container to keep it for later.
senses.example: We can peaches to eat in winter.

senses.definition: A waterway made by people to carry boats or to move water.
senses.example: A small boat traveled along a canal between gardens.

senses.definition: To decide that a planned event or order will stop or will no longer happen.
senses.example: The coach had to cancel practice because of lightning.

senses.definition: A piece of wax with a string through it that can be lit to give light.
senses.example: The candle on the cake had a tiny flame.

senses.definition: A strong, heavy cloth used for things such as bags, tents, and paintings.
senses.example: The artist painted a river on the canvas.

senses.definition: A device that stores energy by keeping opposite electric charges apart.
senses.example: A camera flash can take a quick burst of energy from a capacitor.

senses.definition: A tiny tube where materials can pass between blood and nearby tissue.
senses.example: The red blood cell passes through a narrow capillary.

senses.definition: The city or town where a country’s or state’s main government is based.
senses.example: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts.

senses.definition: An uppercase form of a letter, such as A instead of a.
senses.example: Our teacher reminded us to start a name with a capital.

senses.definition: Money or property available to start or run a business.
senses.example: The farmers used some of their capital to buy a new tractor.

senses.definition: Written words that help explain a picture or tell what you would hear in a video.
senses.example: A caption told the viewer that a phone was ringing.

senses.definition: A hard covering over all or part of an animal’s back.
senses.example: The loggerhead’s top shell, called a carapace, is reddish brown.

senses.definition: A group of travelers who make part of a trip together, often carrying goods.
senses.example: The caravan carried salt across the desert.

senses.definition: A type of material that includes sugars, starches, and many kinds of fiber.
senses.example: Oatmeal contains more than one kind of carbohydrate.

senses.definition: A gas whose molecules each contain one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. You release some of it when you breathe out.
senses.example: Carbon dioxide moves from the blood into the air inside your lungs.

senses.definition: To feel concern or interest for someone or something.
senses.example: I care about keeping our classroom tidy.

senses.definition: Attention or help given to keep someone or something safe or well.
senses.example: Our neighbor took care of the cat while we were away.

senses.definition: Attention to how you do something so you avoid trouble or mistakes.
senses.example: Carry the full bowl with care.

senses.definition: Paying attention to avoid mistakes, trouble, or harm.
senses.example: Be careful when you turn the corner with the full tray.

senses.definition: Adapted to get food or nutrients by eating animals.
senses.example: A carnivorous plant can catch a fly in a modified leaf.

senses.definition: To hold or support something while taking it from one place to another.
senses.example: I can carry the empty box upstairs.

senses.definition: To have, hold, or pass something along.
senses.example: The radio signal can carry the music across town.

senses.definition: A tough, bendy body material found in places such as your ears and joints.
senses.example: Cartilage covers the ends of the bones at many joints.

senses.definition: Money in the form of bills or coins.
senses.example: I paid cash instead of using a card.

senses.definition: To exchange a check or similar paper for money.
senses.example: My aunt went to the bank to cash a check.

senses.definition: To stop and hold something that is moving through the air or trying to get away.
senses.example: I reached up to catch the ball.

senses.definition: To arrive in time to get on a bus, train, or other ride.
senses.example: We hurried to catch the train.

senses.definition: To figure out how something works or what someone means.
senses.example: I began to catch on after I watched the first two turns of the game.

senses.definition: To become popular or start being used by many people.
senses.example: Our made-up hand clap began to catch on at camp.

senses.definition: To reach someone who went ahead or get to the same stage as someone else.
senses.example: I stopped to tie my shoe, then ran to catch up with the group.

senses.definition: Something that makes an event happen.
senses.example: A loose wheel was the cause of the rattling noise.

senses.definition: An aim that people work to support.
senses.example: The club donated money to a good cause.

senses.definition: To make something happen.
senses.example: Strong wind can cause branches to fall.

senses.definition: A hollow space or, in a tooth, a hole caused by decay.
senses.example: A dentist can check for a cavity.

senses.definition: The inside surface above your head in a room.
senses.example: We hung paper stars from the ceiling.

senses.definition: To do something special to show happiness or honor an event or person.
senses.example: We made a banner to celebrate our last day of school.

senses.definition: A tiny unit that can carry out the basic jobs of life. Living things are made of one or more cells.
senses.example: Under a microscope, we saw many cells in a thin piece of onion skin.

senses.definition: One part of a battery that turns stored chemical energy into electrical energy.
senses.example: Some flashlights use a single battery cell.

senses.definition: One box in a grid or a computer spreadsheet.
senses.example: Type the total in the cell at the bottom of the column.

senses.definition: A small room in a prison or another place where a person lives alone.
senses.example: The old prison cell is now part of a museum tour.

senses.definition: A thin layer around a cell that helps control what goes in and out.
senses.example: The cell membrane separates the watery inside from its surroundings.

senses.definition: An official count of the people who live in a place. The count may also collect other information about them.
senses.example: The United States carries out a census of its population every ten years.

senses.definition: The point that describes where an object’s mass is balanced. It may fall in an empty space within the object.
senses.example: The center of mass of the ring was in the middle of its open space.

senses.definition: A hard material, such as fired clay, usually made from minerals and set by heat.
senses.example: The ceramic in the cup started as soft clay.

senses.definition: Sure that something is true or going to happen.
senses.example: I am certain I left my book on this desk.

senses.definition: A particular one or group, even if it is not named.
senses.example: The room is open only on certain days.

senses.definition: A seat for one person, usually with a back.
senses.example: I put my backpack beside the chair.

senses.definition: The person who leads a group or meeting.
senses.example: The chair asked us to vote on the plan.

senses.definition: To lead a meeting or group.
senses.example: I will chair today’s book club meeting.

senses.definition: A room or an enclosed space inside something.
senses.example: Each chamber in the heart holds blood for part of a heartbeat.

senses.definition: A possibility that something will happen.
senses.example: There is a chance of rain this afternoon.

senses.definition: An opportunity to do something.
senses.example: I had a chance to try the trumpet.

senses.definition: Luck or something that happens without a plan.
senses.example: We met at the park by chance.

senses.definition: To become different or make something different.
senses.example: You may change your answer before turning in the paper.

senses.definition: Something that becomes different, or the difference itself.
senses.example: The cold weather was a big change from yesterday.

senses.definition: Coins, or money returned when you pay more than something costs.
senses.example: I got two dollars in change at the store.

senses.definition: To decide something different from what you decided before.
senses.example: You can still change your mind about which story to read.

senses.definition: A person, animal, or other being who takes part in a story.
senses.example: A curious fox was the main character.

senses.definition: One letter, number, symbol, or other mark in a line of text.
senses.example: The last character in the line is an exclamation mark.

senses.definition: To ask someone to pay a price for something.
senses.example: The store will charge two dollars for the notebook.

senses.definition: To put energy into a battery so it can be used again.
senses.example: I plugged in the tablet to charge it.

senses.definition: A property of matter that can be positive or negative. Charges of the same kind push apart, and opposite kinds pull together.
senses.example: A rubbed balloon can pick up an electric charge and stick to a wall.

senses.definition: To rush forward quickly.
senses.example: The players charged toward the ball.

senses.definition: Responsibility for looking after or managing something.
senses.example: I was in charge of feeding the class fish.

senses.definition: An official document that sets out what a group is for and how it will work.
senses.example: Representatives signed a charter for their new organization.

senses.definition: To hurry after someone or something to try to catch it.
senses.example: The kitten tried to chase a blowing leaf.

senses.definition: An act of hurrying after someone or something.
senses.example: The dog gave up the chase when the ball landed in the pond.

senses.definition: Costing little money.
senses.example: We found a cheap notebook at the store.

senses.definition: Made poorly or with little care.
senses.example: The cheap handle snapped the first time I pulled it.

senses.definition: To look at something carefully to see if it is right or find out about it.
senses.example: Please check that your name is on the paper.

senses.definition: A mark showing that something was chosen or looked at.
senses.example: Put a check by each chore you finish.

senses.definition: A written order asking a bank to pay money to someone.
senses.example: Our club sent a check to the animal shelter.

senses.definition: In chess, a position in which the king is under attack and no legal move can make it safe.
senses.example: The game ended in checkmate.

senses.definition: To shout or clap to show approval or support.
senses.example: We cheered when our friend reached the finish line.

senses.definition: To make someone feel less sad or worried.
senses.example: A visit from my friend helped cheer me up.

senses.definition: A shout or sound of support or happiness.
senses.example: Our group gave a cheer when the lights came back on.

senses.definition: A change in which substances turn into other substances as atoms rearrange.
senses.example: Tiny gas bubbles marked a chemical reaction in the batter.

senses.definition: Making food using energy from chemicals instead of energy from sunlight.
senses.example: Some bacteria at ocean vents use chemosynthesis.

senses.definition: To use your teeth to break food into smaller pieces or to bite something again and again.
senses.example: The horse began to chew the hay.

senses.definition: A young person who has not yet grown into an adult.
senses.example: Each child chose a different color of paper.

senses.definition: A son or daughter of a person, at any age.
senses.example: My father is one of my grandmother’s three children.

senses.definition: A raised garden made from mud, plants, and other materials in shallow water, with canals around it.
senses.example: The farmer reached her chinampa by boat.

senses.definition: A green substance in plants and some other living things that absorbs light used to make sugars.
senses.example: Chlorophyll gives most leaves their green color.

senses.definition: The act of choosing, or something you can choose.
senses.example: We had a choice between tea and water.

senses.definition: To decide which person, thing, or action you want.
senses.example: We can choose one book to take home.

senses.definition: A group of different notes played or heard together as one musical unit.
senses.example: I pressed three keys at once to play a chord.

senses.definition: A long piece of DNA and the proteins that help it fit inside a cell.
senses.example: A body cell usually has more than one chromosome.

senses.definition: A path that electric charge can move through when the path makes a complete loop.
senses.example: Closing the switch completed the circuit and made the toy spin.

senses.definition: A route that brings you back to where you started.
senses.example: We made one circuit of the park before lunch.

senses.definition: A device that opens part of a circuit automatically when more current flows than it is made to carry.
senses.example: When too much current flowed, the circuit breaker opened the path.

senses.definition: Movement around a place or along a path that brings something back again.
senses.example: The movement of blood around the body is called circulation.

senses.definition: The distance around a circle.
senses.example: We used string to measure the circumference of a jar lid.

senses.definition: A city and the land around it that have their own government.
senses.example: Tikal was a Maya city-state.

senses.definition: A large society with a shared way of life and organized systems, often including cities, trade, or government.
senses.example: People in the ancient Maya civilization built cities and developed ways to keep track of time.

senses.definition: To say something is true, sometimes before there is proof.
senses.example: The two teams both claimed they had won.

senses.definition: To ask for or take something that belongs to you.
senses.example: You can claim your jacket at the office.

senses.definition: A statement that something is true or that you have a right to it.
senses.example: We looked for evidence to check the claim.

senses.definition: To strike your hands together, often to keep time or show approval.
senses.example: Clap twice when it is your turn.

senses.definition: A short loud sound, such as one made by hands or thunder.
senses.example: We heard one clap of thunder.

senses.definition: A group of students learning together, or the time they spend learning.
senses.example: Our class is reading a book about the Moon.

senses.definition: A group of things that share certain features.
senses.example: These objects belong to the same class of tools.

senses.definition: Free of dirt, stains, or unwanted material.
senses.example: I took a clean plate from the shelf.

senses.definition: To remove dirt or things that should not be there.
senses.example: We clean the table before setting out food.

senses.definition: Easy to see through or easy to understand.
senses.example: Use clear directions so everyone can find the door.

senses.definition: Free from things that block or fill a place.
senses.example: The front steps are clear of snow.

senses.definition: To remove something that is in the way.
senses.example: Let’s clear the path so people can walk through.

senses.definition: A person whose job includes helping customers or keeping records.
senses.example: The clerk helped me find the right envelope.

senses.definition: Quick at learning, thinking, or finding a smart way to do something.
senses.example: Luz found a clever way to keep the door from swinging shut.

senses.definition: The usual pattern of weather in a place over many years.
senses.example: A place with a dry climate may have a rainy day even though most days are dry.

senses.definition: To go upward, often using your hands and feet.
senses.example: We used the stairs to climb to the attic.

senses.definition: A trip upward that can take effort.
senses.example: The climb to the hilltop took ten minutes.

senses.definition: A tool that shows what time it is.
senses.example: The classroom clock showed ten past two.

senses.definition: To measure or record how long something takes or how fast it goes.
senses.example: The coach clocked each runner.

senses.definition: Near in distance, time, or a relationship.
senses.example: The library is close to my home.

senses.definition: Near someone, something, or a place.
senses.example: Please stay close while we cross the street.

senses.definition: To shut something or bring it to an end.
senses.example: We close the gate after the last person comes in.

senses.definition: The end of an event or period of time.
senses.example: At the close of the show, everyone clapped.

senses.definition: A lump that forms when pieces and materials in blood stick together.
senses.example: A clot may close a small cut.

senses.definition: One of the separate parts packed together in a garlic bulb.
senses.example: The cook peeled a clove of garlic.

senses.definition: A piece of information that helps you find something or solve a problem.
senses.example: A muddy footprint gave us a clue.

senses.definition: The land along the edge of an ocean or sea.
senses.example: Our train followed the coast for an hour.

senses.definition: To keep moving without adding power or pedaling.
senses.example: I let the bike coast down the gentle hill.

senses.definition: A curled part of the inner ear that helps change sound vibrations into signals the brain can use.
senses.example: Tiny hair cells in the cochlea move when waves pass through its liquid.

senses.definition: An artwork made by attaching pieces of paper, cloth, or other material to a surface.
senses.example: The class made a collage out of old maps and scraps of paper.

senses.definition: To gather things together or get something that is waiting for you.
senses.example: We collect fallen leaves for an art project.

senses.definition: To gather a certain kind of thing over time because you like it.
senses.example: My uncle likes to collect old stamps.

senses.definition: A group of things that have been gathered together.
senses.example: My aunt has a collection of old postcards.

senses.definition: A place controlled by another country, often after people from that country settle there.
senses.example: Massachusetts was once a British colony.

senses.definition: The way light makes something look red, blue, green, or another shade.
senses.example: Yellow was the brightest color in the mural.

senses.definition: To find or meet something or someone by chance.
senses.example: You might come across a sketch Dad drew between the pages of that book.

senses.definition: To think of something that solves a problem or adds an idea.
senses.example: We had to come up with a way to carry six cups without spilling them.

senses.definition: An icy object that travels around the Sun and can grow glowing tails of gas and dust as it warms up.
senses.example: The comet grew a bright tail as it drew near the Sun.

senses.definition: A feeling of being at ease, or something that makes a hard time easier.
senses.example: My favorite story brought me comfort when I was sick.

senses.definition: To help someone feel less worried, sad, or hurt.
senses.example: A quiet word helped comfort my friend.

senses.definition: Seen or happening often.
senses.example: A robin is a common sight in our neighborhood.

senses.definition: Used or shared by two or more people or things.
senses.example: Everyone in the room worked toward a common goal.

senses.definition: A bottom number that can be used for two or more fractions without changing their values.
senses.example: Six is a common denominator for one half and one third because they can be written as three sixths and two sixths.

senses.definition: A rule that says swapping two numbers being added or multiplied leaves the answer the same.
senses.example: By the commutative property, five times eight equals eight times five.

senses.definition: To look at two or more things to see how they are alike or different.
senses.example: We compared the two maps to see which streets had changed.

senses.definition: To tell someone that you are unhappy about something.
senses.example: A few riders complained about the long wait.

senses.definition: Finished or having every part it needs.
senses.example: The puzzle is complete now that we found the last piece.

senses.definition: To finish doing or making something.
senses.example: We need one more drawing to complete the poster.

senses.definition: A person who creates a piece of music.
senses.example: The composer wrote a different part for each instrument.

senses.definition: A dark mixture formed after scraps from plants and other living things break down.
senses.example: The finished compost was mixed with soil near the flowers.

senses.definition: A substance made of atoms from at least two different elements chemically joined in a fixed proportion.
senses.example: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

senses.definition: A way to store or send information in less space than it took before.
senses.example: Compression made my photo file smaller.

senses.definition: The change from a gas to a liquid. It can happen when water vapor touches something cooler.
senses.example: Condensation made tiny drops on the outside of my cold glass.

senses.definition: Something that has to be true for a rule or action to apply.
senses.example: Our game ends if one player reaches ten points. Reaching ten points is the condition.

senses.definition: How something is doing or what kind of shape it is in.
senses.example: The bicycle was old but still in good condition.

senses.definition: In a program, instructions that are used only if a particular test has the right result.
senses.example: The game uses a conditional to check whether I reached the end.

senses.definition: The movement of heat or electricity through something, such as through a metal spoon.
senses.example: The spoon handle warmed by conduction after the bowl of the spoon touched the soup.

senses.definition: A material that lets electricity or heat move through it easily.
senses.example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.

senses.definition: A person who leads a group of musicians as they play or sing.
senses.example: We watched the conductor for the signal to start playing.

senses.definition: A person who helps run a train and may check passengers’ tickets.
senses.example: The conductor announced the next stop.

senses.definition: A solid shape with a round or other closed base and sides that narrow to a single point.
senses.example: The paper party hat looked like a cone.

senses.definition: A cell in the eye that helps you see colors and details in enough light.
senses.example: Different cone cells can respond more strongly to different colors of light.

senses.definition: Feeling sure that you can do something or that something is true.
senses.example: I felt confident that I could read the poem aloud.

senses.definition: To make it hard for someone to understand or tell things apart.
senses.example: The missing sign may confuse people looking for the exit.

senses.definition: To mix up two things and think one is the other.
senses.example: I confuse those two street names because they sound alike.

senses.definition: To join two or more things or make a link between them.
senses.example: Connect the dots to make a picture.

senses.definition: The basic rules that describe how a government is organized and what it can do. A constitution can also protect people’s rights.
senses.example: The United States Constitution sets out the jobs of the three branches of the national government.

senses.definition: One of the largest land areas into which people divide Earth. Different maps sometimes group them in different ways.
senses.example: A map can show the continent of Africa and the countries within it.

senses.definition: To keep doing something or to start it again after a pause.
senses.example: We will continue the story tomorrow.

senses.definition: A line on a map that joins places at the same height.
senses.example: One contour line curved all the way around the hill.

senses.definition: To guide what something does or keep it within limits.
senses.example: These buttons control the fan speed.

senses.definition: The power to guide something, or a device that lets you do it.
senses.example: The volume control is on the right side of the screen.

senses.definition: The way a gas or liquid carries heat as it moves from place to place.
senses.example: Convection carried warmer water toward the top of the pot.

senses.definition: One of the numbers that describes the position of a point on a map or grid.
senses.example: The first coordinate in (5, 2) tells how far right to go.

senses.definition: A small ocean animal with a soft, tube-shaped body. Many corals live in groups and make hard structures that can build up into reefs.
senses.example: Fish sheltered among the branches of a coral.

senses.definition: A pinkish orange color.
senses.example: I mixed pink and orange paint to make coral.

senses.definition: Damage to a material after it reacts with substances around it, such as air or moisture.
senses.example: A coat of paint can protect a steel bridge from corrosion.

senses.definition: A weight used to balance another weight or make it easier to move around.
senses.example: A counterweight balances much of the weight of the elevator car.

senses.definition: The strength to do something even if it feels scary or hard.
senses.example: It took courage to ask for help in front of the group.
